course.description: fix: it blocks the reporting step, is related or is critical - the run's recovery fixes it at its root now. list: none of these holds - it is added to the run's list of pre-existing issues, shown at the end. duplicate: the list already holds it, and duplicates names its id. unproven: you could not reproduce it on the base commit - it is not listed.

title.description: One line a person who never saw the run understands: what is wrong, and where.

description.description: What is wrong, where, and what it causes, from what your proof shows and nothing else.

where.description: The paths, from the repository's root, or the command, where the issue is.

proof.description: What you read or ran on the base commit that shows the issue.

kind.description: read: you read a file at the base commit. ran: you ran a command there. none: you could not reproduce it, and the course is unproven.

at.description: The base commit you checked it at.

file.description: For read, the path from the repository's root; otherwise empty.

lines.description: For read, the lines, as 12-19; otherwise empty.

quote.description: For read, those lines word for word; otherwise empty.

command.description: For ran, the command word for word; otherwise empty.

output.description: For ran, what it printed that shows the issue, word for word; for none, what you tried; otherwise empty.

blocks.description: True only where the reporting step said it stops its own work and your check confirms it.

related.description: True where the issue is in a path the plan's items change or depend on, or in the behaviour the request asks for.

critical.description: True where, on the base commit, it loses data, opens a security hole, crashes, or keeps the build or the tests from passing.

why.description: Why the course: which test held and what shows it; for list, that none held.

duplicates.description: For duplicate, the id of the listed issue it repeats; otherwise empty.
